newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan utility tenders for uranium supplies.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan utility tenders for uranium supplies.

text.p: State utility Taiwan Power Co has invited bids for up to 750,000 pounds (340,000 kg) of uranium a year to fire its three nuclear power plants -- imports that could alarm rival China.
The deadline for bids for two three-year contracts is 0830 GMT on February 27, with the winning bid expected to be selected on February 28, a Taipower official confirmed on Friday.
Both supply contracts specify shipments to be delivered to Taiwan in September 1997, March 1998 and March 1999.

China, Taiwan's arch rival since a civil war split them in 1949, has voiced concern over earlier Taiwan uranium imports, saying the substance was no "ordinary commodity" and calling its export to Taiwan a highly sensitive issue.

Taipower officials said uranium-rich Australia was unlikely to participate in the bidding. Australia bans export of uranium to Taiwan due to differences between government nuclear safety regulations but Canberra has said it was studying whether uranium could be sold to Taipei under Taiwan's existing safeguards
Bids for Taipower's uranium tenders must comply with the safeguards framework that Taiwan reached in 1971 with the International Atomic Energy Agency and the United States, utility officials said.
Taipower has three nuclear power stations, each with two operating reactors, which consume a total of 2.5 million pounds of uranium fuel rods a year.
Canada, the United States and Namibia have been Taipower's main uranium suppliers.
Taipower has a fourth nuclear power station under construction in northern Taipei county.

Taipower signed a contract on January 11 with North Korea under which it can ship up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea, an arrangement that has sparked protests from Pyongyang's rival South Korea. The company plans to ship 60,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea in the first two years.
